type: theorem: ∀ hf : Function.Injective f, ∀ d P, hasseDeriv (d.mapDomain f) (rename f P) = rename f (hasseDeriv d P)
what: Hasse derivatives commute with injective variable renaming when the multi-index is transported along the same injection.
how: Monomial/additive induction; binomial product transport and mapDomain truncated subtraction compatibility.
hypotheses: Independent arbitrary variable types σ/τ, CommSemiring R, any injective f, finite multi-index d and polynomial P.
caller_summary: One explicit call in Roth.hasseDeriv_rename_mul_aeval, Separation165; no internal uses; indirect Separation365 not counted.
mathlib_api_audit: Pinned pderiv_rename is first-order analogue; Finsupp.prod_mapDomain_index_inj/mapDomain_apply_of_injective/mapDomain_tsub supply individual monomial transports, not full Hasse identity.
moral_duplications: No verified direct replacement; standard all-order extension of first-order injective renaming law.
generalization: Actual collision counterexample proves global injectivity cannot simply be dropped; support-local injectivity plausible but no verified weakening. Embedding/square variants equivalent; literal Semiring interfaces fail.
missing_api: Injective-renaming naturality for all multivariate divided derivative orders.
action: YES-add-as-is; group with accepted multivariate Hasse parent/coefficient/map API in Mathlib/Algebra/MvPolynomial/HasseDeriv.lean; generalise/cleanup and fresh duplicate check before PR.
